title: China'sclimatechange commitment
content:
1. China has become increasingly active in international climate discussions. It recently announced ambitious emissions reduction goals.

2. China's climate commitments are driven by two key factors. First and foremost is the well-being of the Chinese people. China has made a variety of moves and policies to deal with climate change, which will benefit the Chinese people. Needless to say, sustainable development, or "ecological civilization," is a key policy aim.

3. The second source of motivation is international responsibility. China sent a strong message to the international community by helping to negotiate and then signing the Paris Agreement on climate change. For that reason, China is committed to cutting its carbon emissions by 60-65 percent from 2005 levels by 2030. These actions show China's commitment to playing a bigger role in reducing global warming.

4. From an environmental perspective, the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions will benefit China's "war on pollution," energy transformation, resource conservation and ecosystem restoration. One of China's domestic policies focuses on energy conservation. Enhanced heat efficiency in coal-fired power generation is one way to help meet this policy goal.

5. The share of "dirty" coal is also being reduced. Cleaner and lower-carbon fuels are replacing coal as a source of energy. In the past decade, China has become the world's largest market for hydropower, nuclear, wind and solar energy. Many policies have been introduced to aid the growth of forests and reclaim deserts. Efforts also target at absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and at improving local ecosystems.

6. China's economic transformation will aid its efforts to battle climate change. To a certain degree, a post-industrialized, service economy will help control carbon dioxide emissions. It goes without saying that China cannot achieve a high level of modernization without world-class innovation and technology. Because climate change is a new problem, it provides a key opportunity for China's innovation. China has established strong technology and production capabilities in low-carbon energy sectors. Wind turbines and solar panels have increased clean energy use in China to 12 percent, higher than that of the United States.

7. Clean energy sources will also help address regional economic differences. Areas that have sufficient wind and solar resources are often poorer and more difficult to reach. By using wind and solar power, these regions will see significant job gains. Already, more than 2.5 million people work in the solar power sector alone in China, compared with 260,000 people in the United States.

8. From a social perspective, limiting carbon dioxide emissions promotes more sustainable urban living. Smarter urban planning, as well as the development of low-carbon cities and provinces, is already contributing to reducing demand for private transport and energy.

9. China is a country prone to natural disasters, many of which are related to the climate. Combating climate change may help to reduce the impact of such disasters. Moreover, climate change policies can help reduce poverty by providing better access to energy through use of renewables.

10. International climate commitments are an important part of China's priorities. On the whole, China views climate change reduction as an opportunity, not a burden. Lowering carbon emissions and energy conservation brings both health and economic benefits to the Chinese people. This commitment and progress has received global recognition.
